messages.subject: Re: Applying shape files
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Well, I am not sure if I understood your question. But you did right loading back the shape file to R (new pic script):

library(raster)
library(FIELDimageR)
library(rgdal)

ShapeFile <- readOGR("Other_Software_ShapeFile.shp")

plot(ShapeFile)

However to overlayer the same shape file to two different pictures it is super important remember that these two pictures must have the same geographic position (GCPs) and the same rotation theta (fieldRotate function). If you follow those rules the Shapefile should work well. Then you can 1) rotate (fieldRotate), 2) remove the soil if is necessary (fieldMask), 3) calculate vegetation indices (fieldIndex), and 4) extract data (fieldInfo). You do not need to draw the shapefile again (fieldShape).
Is that make sense?

Please see more information in this tutorial:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2khnveYFov8
https://phenome-force.github.io/FIELDimageR-workshop/

Let me know if it works..!!!
All the best,
Filipe

messages.subject_clean: CAN I SAVE SHAPEFILE FILE GENERATED WITH FIELDimageR
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I have drone images of a peanut field taken at different stages of crop growth. I have also done the mosaicking using WebODM. However, I realized it is easier to accurately design the shapefile using FIELDimageR at the initial growth stages compared to when there is total canopy cover.

So I want to find out whether I can save the shapefile from the initial plant growth analysis using FIELDimageR, and then re-import it to analyze the images taken around maturity so I don't struggle to regenerate the shapefile again.

Thank you,
Kassim.
https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3994-5066
Creative data analysis will help the discovery of new plant traits and approaches to plant improvement.....###CSSA

messages.body_plain:
Hi Kassim,

Thank you for asking..!!!
Definitely, it is exactly what I am doing in my research. I draw the shapefile using one mosaic from initial growth stage and I import it back every time that I need to extract information from other stages.

More information at: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P17

library(rgdal)

# Saving shapefile.
writeOGR(fieldShape, ".", "fieldShape", driver="ESRI Shapefile")

# Reading the saved shapefile.
fieldShape.2 <- readOGR("fieldShape.shp")

Let me know if this information helped you...!!!
All the best,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: Some questions on FIELDImageR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Evrard,

Thank you for asking.

I will try to answer your questions, but I appreciate some help to complement those from other members in our community.

1-The package doesn't come in R studio from internet?

Answer: Yes, the package does not is installed by default in RStudio. You need to install FIELDimageR in your computer by following one of the options available here: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#Instal

2-Counting is easy with align species with the package but what if I'm in real situation with unaligned tree species, how can I train the model to know the species that i'm working on?

Answer: The algorithm used in function fieldCount is based on image segmentation followed by the pixels distance matrix evaluation. We do not train a model in this strategy (it is not a machine learning method). To use this function and get good results it is important keep in mind that the objects (trees) should not touch each other, which it is super hard in natural landscapes as yours. The only way to get better results is if you choose/create a vegetation index that allows better separation among trees during the remove soil step (function fieldMask).

3-Is there anyway to count multiple tree species at a time or should I do it one by one if the problem at 2- is solved?

Answer: Following the answer above at question 2. You can select specific vegetation index and thresholding to identify each specie in your field (fieldMask and fieldIndex functions). And stead count the number of plants, you can use the function fieldArea to evaluate the percentage covered by each specie. Similar to what I did with different colors of seeds in this example here https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P8 , but in your case are different species.

4-Using the DSM0 is easy when dealing with plant or horticultural species, but what if we are dealing with tree that have been there before drone image collection, is there any way to remove the vegetation so we have the soil only?

Answer: One possible solution is to use the file called DTM (Digital Terrain Model) as soil base and the file DSM (Digital Surface Model) as trees coverage. The Canopy Height Model is calculated by CHM=DSM-DTM. Better explanation about differences between these files is on minute 45 of this video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U-bsA7QjzYE&t=1116s. The pipeline how to use FIELDimageR to calculate and extract CHP is available here https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P10 .

Please, let me know if you have any other question and if the answers above helped you…!

All the best,

Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi Seba and Gaston,

Thank you for asking. FIELDimageR use as base the package "raster" with allows work with different images formats (e.g. jpg, tif, png, etc).

My guessing is when you change the format from JPG to Tiff you are losing important configurations in your images and the software can't read it.

What about you try to use the original format and see if it works better.

Also, you can reduce the image resolution using the function aggregate: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P20

new_image<-aggregate(previous_image, fact=4)

Let me know if it worked,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: Rotation of orthophoto
messages.body_plain:
Hi Pedja,

I guess it is only a visualization artifect.
The image is similar to the first one, however with the plot orientation straight.
The average result per plot should be the same.

To make a test, you can use the function fieldPolygon to draw a shapefile in the same region (same plots) in both images. Then, you can use the function fiendInfo to extract the data and compare it.

Here is the link showing how to do it: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P15

Let me know if the results changed.
Best
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: Rotation of orthophoto
messages.body_plain:
Hi Pedja,

Maybe the images have different geographical references or they were taken in different days. Are you using GCPs for overlay images?

This error is because your shapefile=EX1 is selecting region outside of mosaic=DEM0 dimentions (shapefile must be smaller and inside the mosaic). Are you sure that you are using the same  rotation theta in both images (EX1 and DEM)? Also, EX1 and DEM are from the same processes of orthomosaicing (because this two images must have the same geographic reference)?

And yes, you can use jpg images as field shape for DEM.

All the best,
Filipe
